correctness.rationale: For X={−1,0,1}, statistic T(x)=x, f∈C² strictly convex with f(1)=0 and f″(1)=c>0, inverse/implicit function theorems give the normalized local f-exponential tangent q_x'(0)=λ_x(x−m)/c. Differentiation of D_f(μ||q) in its second argument yields (1/c)∑λ_x(x−m)h(μ_x/λ_x) with h=f−uf', h'=-u f″. For all same-mean (λ,μ), choose asymmetrically perturbed reference λ(ε)=(s+ε/2,1−2s,s−ε/2), μ=λ+(t,−2t,t). Differentiating the zero stationary sum at ε=0 gives h(x)−h(y)=(x−y)h'(x), x=1+t/s>1, y=1−2t/(1−2s)<1. Every x>1,y<1 is attained by s=(1−y)/(2(x−y)),t=s(x−1), so differentiation in y forces h'(x)=h'(y) constant; thus f″=c/u and f(u)=c u logu+β(u−1). Conversely KL has a strictly convex one-dimensional exponential-family projection objective, minimized at matching mean. A nonconstant binary statistic and normalization determine the law, proving minimal three outcomes. Independent exact rational sample for Pearson chi-square gives nonzero derivative −33/5120 whereas KL gives zero; finite check is not universal proof.

value.rationale: A minimum-information experiment that distinguishes KL from all other nondegenerate smooth f-divergences is a natural question in information geometry. Showing that one fixed three-outcome support and only first-order stationarity, rather than universally varying the support or demanding a full global projection identity, suffices is an independently useful and sharp diagnostic. Binary minimality gives mathematical reason for the exact support size.
